To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sense of body-ownership influences the perception of self-orientation.

body ownership shapes self- orientation perception, presumably by enhancing the weight of visual cues over vestibular signals, and this is a necessary ability that heavily depends on vestibular information.
the perception of self-orientation is influenced by body ownership.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sense of body, a fundamental aspect of self-awareness.
the question of how the sense of one’s body affects the ability to perceive the orientation of one’s own self.
the role of the sense of body in self-orientation perception in everyday life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
body ownership is necessary for a correct perception of self-orientation, and that this is mediated by the weighting of visual information over gravitational information.
body ownership influences the weighting of the vestibular system over the visual system in the process of perceiving self-orientation.
body ownership is a necessary prerequisite for perceiving self-orientation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the body is an important factor for the sense of self and that the sense of self is an important factor in the sense of body.
self-orientation perception is determined by a balance between the visual and vestibular cues and that body ownership affects the weighting of visual over vestibular cues.
self-orientation perception is based on an integration of visual and vestibular signals, and this integration can be influenced by the sense of body-ownership.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sense of body is crucial in the process of determining self-orientation.
the body is not only the center of the visual scene but also of one’s own orientation perception.
the sense of body is a necessary condition for perceiving the self-orientation.
